answer: Before an agent can submit a trade, it must lock a stake in a public contract and bind its identity to a unique, rate-limited credential. Peers score completed trades; proven fraud triggers slashing, while honest history gradually lowers future fees. A sybil operator can still create many identities, but each must fund a separate stake and earn trust through real work. The gale of new accounts meets a velvet barrier: every fake costs capital, time, and a whisper of plausible behavior.
